analysis: The PR changes only CHANGELOG.md (CHANGELOG.md:1-8 in the patch). It adds an Unreleased entry saying `darkbloom update` and `darkbloom restart` now wait up to 60 s for launchd to release the drained job before bootstrapping again, and that a failed relaunch re-arms the watchdog when auto-restart is on. The diff contains no executable code, configuration or schema changes. The provider source implementing this relaunch behaviour (likely the update and restart CLI path, the launchd bootstrap code and the watchdog) was not supplied, so I could not review it. The existing definitions it may touch are T-043 (watchdog rollback authority is the replaceable provider binary), T-013, TB-003 and T-057 (a provider stranded without authorization after a failed restart). A watchdog that re-arms after a failed relaunch is availability-oriented. The next review pass should check whether the actual source change in that code introduces a restart loop, a TOCTOU gap in the launchd label handling, or a bypass of drain semantics. Based on this changelog-only diff, I found no security regression and no threat-model assumption invalidated. The coverage limit is that the implementation is not visible here, so the claim is documentation-only. needs_deeper_review is true only because the implementation is not visible.
